event.summary: Removing tmux sink and output-reap barriers does not leave replacement grid readers overlapping
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

## TLDR
Considered whether removing terminal-output cleanup barriers lets reconnects overlap readers or leave terminal work stalled. The replacement viewer path has no per-viewer external reader or process, and explicitly stops its old sender before installing its replacement, so this is not a finding.

## Details
Assigned patch lines 1-601 delete wait_for_output_reaps and the tmux session-sink open, candidate, reap, readiness, and registry methods; lines 684 onward remove their tests. At the reviewed revision service/handlers.rs:1688-1716 resolves a HostTerminal and requires grid capability; 1739 and 1847-1885 serialize removal and join every displaced/incumbent sender under attachments; 1935-1966 starts only HostAttach and GridSender around the already-owned terminal. service/grid_stream.rs:937-963 gives shutdown priority over the stream and reports completion synchronously; 1169-1175 signals the old input pump on drop, and 1209-1228 gives cancellation priority even during a handover. service/terminals.rs:431-461 and 478-483 hold only an in-process sender/input side. Thus deleting the tmux process-reap proof does not remove the grid sender's own cutover proof. This conclusion concerns the assigned deletion, not a claim that every grid/runtime behavior is correct.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md:1963-1976 says every terminal is a host and old tmux terminals end at startup; 2175-2224 describes host switch points and grid-only attachments. SPEC_impl.md:2885-2888 states exactly: 'The running supervisor runs no tmux at all, and its driver of the old terminals is gone: what remains is the startup step that ends them (below), and the installation's tmux policy after it.' The source refutation above, rather than specification acceptance alone, settles the proposed overlap.

Suggested bucket: other (rejected candidate; no established impact). Confidence: confirmed by source and contract analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation: replacement attachments do not open tmux control clients, and their old grid sender is joined before replacement installation. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not searched. Could-be-highest: false; this candidate establishes no route to security impact or lost user-owned work. Caveats: input already handed to the shared runtime is runtime-owned; this record does not assert cancellation retracts such input.

event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

## TLDR
Considered whether removal of the pane-death latch and its test loses an exit notification while a viewer is busy, or applies an old exit to a restarted agent. The surviving host runtime stores its own monotone liveness and sends exits through a queued notifier; the old tmux pane-identity latch is not needed for that path. No defect is reported.

## Details
Assigned patch lines 605-648 delete a test of PaneDeath::observed_in against a whole-server tmux pane map, its watch latch, and a fresh latch after reattach. That map is no longer a source of terminal death. At the reviewed revision hosts/terminal.rs:3932-3941 first flushes and publishes final output, then sets Liveness::Exited from this runtime's HostEvent::Exited; 4031-4055 retains only forward liveness changes in the runtime's own watch state and enqueues the notification. hosts/terminal.rs:904 and 916 identify the notifier as an unbounded mpsc sender/receiver, so being temporarily busy does not discard the event. These are per-host runtime objects, not lookup of a reusable pane number. service/handlers.rs:1775-1797 also rejects a stale attachment when its generation or terminal changed. SPEC_impl.md:2126-2130 says exit is established only after processing the stream exit record, after drained output, and exits/end/loss notify a shared waiter; 2210-2218 describes the ticker's exit observation. This preserves the role of the removed test through a different mechanism, rather than retaining the retired tmux identity contract.

Suggested bucket: other (rejected candidate; no established impact). Confidence: confirmed by source and contract analysis; no runtime behavior was observed. proposed_drop: source refutation: runtime-specific retained liveness and queued notification replace the removed tmux pane-map latch. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not read. Could-be-highest: false; no security or loss-of-work route is established by this candidate. Caveats: this is not a claim of complete exit-observer test coverage, and does not review unrelated defects in the retired tmux implementation.
